players.product: ArF immersion, ArF dry, KrF and i-line semiconductor lithography systems (NSR series), FPD lithography systems and digital lithography systems for advanced packaging

quarterly_data.quarter: Nikon results presentation: Financial Results for the 1st Quarter of the Year Ending March 31, 2027 (08-06-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CFO Matsumoto: Q1 FY2027/3 Precision Equipment revenue rose 4.4 billion yen to 38.2 billion yen; semiconductor lithography system sales rose by 3 units to 5 units, driven by ArF dry systems, while FPD lithography system sales fell by 2 units to 5 as some installations were postponed to Q2. The segment swung to an operating loss of 2.6 billion yen, mainly due to 4.1 billion yen of inventory write-downs caused by a long-term stagnation of equipment resulting from a timing discrepancy in customer orders.
quarterly_data.figure: Precision Equipment revenue 38.2 billion yen (+4.4); semiconductor lithography 5 units; FPD lithography 5 units; inventory write-downs 4.1 billion yen

quarterly_data.quarter: Nikon results presentation: Financial Results for the 1st Quarter of the Year Ending March 31, 2027 (08-06-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CFO Matsumoto: in Q1 Nikon completed installation and recognized revenue for its new ArF dry lithography system, the NSR-S333F (first sale).

quarterly_data.quarter: Nikon results presentation: Financial Results for the 1st Quarter of the Year Ending March 31, 2027 (08-06-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CFO Matsumoto: the FY2027/3 Precision Equipment forecast is unchanged at revenue 188.0 billion yen (+20.8 billion YoY) and operating profit 12.0 billion yen, as lower FPD lithography unit sales are offset by higher ArF dry and immersion lithography unit sales; the majority of the Q1 inventory write-down is expected to be recovered through order intake in the second half. Nikon plans 23 new and 6 refurbished semiconductor lithography systems (market scale 580 units) and 27 FPD lithography systems in the year.
quarterly_data.figure: Precision Equipment revenue 188.0 billion yen, OP 12.0 billion yen; 23 new / 6 refurbished semiconductor lithography units; 27 FPD units

quarterly_data.quarter: Nikon results presentation: Financial Results for the 1st Quarter of the Year Ending March 31, 2027 (08-06-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CFO Matsumoto: Q1 revenue was 164.1 billion yen (+6.0 billion YoY) with an operating loss of 0.9 billion yen, as US tariff refunds of 4.0 billion yen offset the Precision Equipment inventory write-downs; the full-year operating profit forecast was raised by 1.0 billion yen to 11.0 billion yen on revenue of 732.0 billion yen.
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 revenue 164.1 billion yen; FY operating profit forecast 11.0 billion yen; FY revenue forecast 732.0 billion yen

quarterly_data.quarter: Nikon results presentation: Financial Results for the 1st Quarter of the Year Ending March 31, 2027 (08-06-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CFO Matsumoto: Industry Business Q1 revenue rose 2.8 billion yen to 17.9 billion yen on higher and accelerated shipments of optical components and imaging measurement systems for electronic components and semiconductor applications; full-year revenue was revised up by 4.0 billion yen, and revenue should grow on higher sales of EUV-related components and other customized products.
quarterly_data.figure: Industry revenue 17.9 billion yen (+2.8); FY revenue forecast raised 4.0 billion yen

Nikon.why: Makes ArF immersion, ArF dry, KrF and i-line semiconductor lithography systems plus EUV-related components and digital lithography for advanced packaging; its Precision Equipment growth this year rests on ArF dry and immersion unit sales to chipmakers.
Nikon.evidence: Nikon results presentation: Financial Results for the 1st Quarter of the Year Ending March 31, 2027 (08-06-2026): revenue should increase as the decline in FPD lithography system unit sales is offset by an increase in ArF lithography system unit sales; in the first quarter, we completed installation and recognized the related revenue for our new ArF dry lithography system, the NSR-S333F.
